```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the tour and the bench drivers:
# the source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a
# bare installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# The five-minute path runs against committed test bytes only: the specimen
# fixture (tests/testthat/fixtures/sigprofiler_sbs96_specimen.txt) plus the
# bundled reference face shipped inside the package. No downloads, no real
# data -- the claims-are-measured law of the docs/site lanes.
FIX <- local({
  if (is.na(PKG)) stop("fixture face requires the source checkout")
  fp <- file.path(PKG, "tests", "testthat", "fixtures",
                  "sigprofiler_sbs96_specimen.txt")
  if (!file.exists(fp)) stop("specimen fixture missing: ", fp)
  fp
})
```

## Install

msuiter is a source install: the numerical kernels are a Rust workspace that
`R CMD INSTALL` builds through the package `configure` face, so the toolchain
floors stated in DESCRIPTION bind the install itself. The committed renv
lockfile pins the R and package universe the campaign is validated against;
restoring it before installing keeps the floor question answered by bytes
rather than by luck.

```{r install-face}
if (!is.na(PKG)) {
  desc <- readLines(file.path(PKG, "DESCRIPTION"), warn = FALSE)
  print(desc[grepl("^Package:|^Version:|^Depends:|^SystemRequirements:",
                   desc)])
  lockfile <- file.path(PKG, "docs", "paper", "renv.lock")
  if (file.exists(lockfile)) {
    print(basename(lockfile))
  } else if (!dir.exists(file.path(PKG, "docs", "paper"))) {
    # The check/tarball build face: docs/ is a repository tree that
    # .Rbuildignore withholds from the source package -- the lockfile is
    # then simply outside this build context, said here rather than
    # stopped on. In the site/lane render (docs/ present) the branch
    # above must speak; its absence there would be a real defect.
    print("renv.lock: repository-tree face -- outside the source-package build context")
  } else {
    stop("committed renv lockfile missing from its own committed directory")
  }
} else {
  print("install face reads the source DESCRIPTION")
}
```

With the floors met, the install face is one command:

```{sh, eval = FALSE}
R CMD INSTALL msuiter   # from the source root; configure builds the Rust core
```

## Five-minute path

One chain, four faces, end to end: `ms_variants()` validates the typed input
IR, `ms_tally()` runs it through the Rust kernel over a micro twoBit genome
into a channel table, `ms_signature()` mounts the committed specimen matrix as
a signature dictionary pinned to that channel table, and the bundled
reference face arrives as an `MsRefDb` -- the COSMIC v3.6 dictionaries ship
inside the package, so the trusted default needs no download.

The genome is the same synthetic writer the tour uses: a trivial chromosome
whose bases agree with the variant records base for base, so every printed
number below is real kernel output over committed bytes.

```{r genome}
.u32le <- function(v) writeBin(as.integer(v), raw(), size = 4L,
                               endian = "little")
.pack_bases <- function(bases) {
  out <- raw((length(bases) + 3L) %/% 4L)
  acc <- 0L; filled <- 0L; k <- 0L
  for (b in bases) {
    acc <- bitwOr(bitwShiftL(acc, 2L), b); filled <- filled + 1L
    if (filled == 4L) { k <- k + 1L; out[k] <- as.raw(acc); acc <- 0L; filled <- 0L }
  }
  if (filled > 0L) out[k + 1L] <- as.raw(bitwShiftL(acc, 2L * (4L - filled)))
  out
}
.write_2bit <- function(path) {
  chr1 <- rep(c(2L, 1L), 32L)
  chr2 <- rep(c(3L, 1L), 20L)
  recs <- list(
    list(name = "chr1", size = 64L, dna = .pack_bases(chr1),
         nb = integer(0), nl = integer(0)),
    list(name = "chr2", size = 40L, dna = .pack_bases(chr2),
         nb = integer(0), nl = integer(0)))
  off <- 16L + sum(vapply(recs, function(r) 1L + nchar(r$name) + 4L, 0L))
  index <- raw(); body <- raw()
  for (r in recs) {
    index <- c(index, as.raw(nchar(r$name)), charToRaw(r$name), .u32le(off))
    rec <- c(.u32le(r$size), .u32le(length(r$nb)), .u32le(r$nb), .u32le(r$nl),
             .u32le(0L), .u32le(0L), r$dna)
    body <- c(body, rec); off <- off + length(rec)
  }
  bytes <- c(.u32le(0x1A412743L), .u32le(0L), .u32le(length(recs)),
             .u32le(0L), index, body)
  con <- file(path, "wb"); on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  writeBin(bytes, con); invisible(path)
}
genome <- file.path(tempdir(), "getstarted-2bit.2bit")
.write_2bit(genome)
```

```{r variants}
tab <- data.frame(
  chrom  = c("chr1", "chr1", "chr1"),
  start  = c(12L, 22L, 14L),
  end    = c(12L, 22L, 14L),
  ref    = c("C", "C", "C"),
  alt    = c("A", "T", "T"),
  sample = c("S1", "S1", "S2"))
v <- ms_variants(tab, "GRCh38", caller = "get-started",
                 matched_normal = "none")
v
```

```{r tally}
cat1 <- ms_tally(v, genome)
cat1
```

The signature dictionary is the committed specimen itself -- read verbatim,
its first two columns mounted under the channel labels the tally produced,
so every exposure figure below is the fixture's own number and the channel
hash is derived from the validated catalog, never hand-forged:

```{r signature}
raw_spec <- utils::read.delim(FIX, check.names = FALSE,
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
labels <- cat1@channels$labels
spec <- as.matrix(raw_spec[, 2L:3L, drop = FALSE])
rownames(spec) <- raw_spec[[1L]]
if (!identical(rownames(spec), labels)) stop("specimen rows must ride the channel labels")
exposures <- matrix(c(0.6, 0.4), 2L, 1L,
                    dimnames = list(colnames(spec), "S1"))
summary1 <- list(
  n_channels   = length(labels), n_samples = 1L,
  channel_name = cat1@channels$name, channel_hash = cat1@channels$hash,
  build = "GRCh38")
sig <- ms_signature(spec, exposures, summary1, engine = "synthetic", seed = 1L)
sig
```

```{r refdb}
br <- ms_refdb_bundled()
db <- br[["SBS_GRCh38"]]
db
head(db@matrices[[1L]][, 1L:3L], 3L)
```

## Anatomy of the output

The `MsSignature` above is a typed object, not a loose matrix: the
signature matrix, the exposure matrix, the pinned channel summary and the
provenance (engine, seed) are separate slots, each validated at the
boundary that owns it.

```{r anatomy}
print(class(sig))
str(sig)
print(dim(sig@signatures))
print(dim(sig@exposures))
print(sig@engine)
print(substr(sig@catalog_summary$channel_hash, 1L, 16L))
```

The channel hash printed above is the tamper seal: it is recomputed from the
validated channel table, and a hand-edited dictionary is refused at
construction -- the same seal the tour demonstrates from the refusing side.
